course.title: JavaScript
course.description: A complete JavaScript course from foundations through advanced language mechanics and production browser engineering. It teaches ECMAScript values, syntax, control flow, functions, data structures, objects, prototypes, classes, errors, testing, asynchronous programming, modules, browser APIs, persistence, advanced iteration/binary/resource features, memory, security, performance, workers, and a realistic offline capstone.
prerequisites: Basic computer literacy and file editing.
A modern browser; Node.js is needed for selected testing/module exercises.
No prior JavaScript experience is required.
learningOutcomes: Write reliable JavaScript with modern syntax and data structures.
Reason about scope, closures, this, prototypes, classes, and metaprogramming.
Design errors, tests, and debugging workflows.
Build robust asynchronous and concurrent workflows.
Use browser APIs safely for DOM, forms, fetch, storage, and IndexedDB.
Use iterators, generators, typed arrays, resource management, memory, workers, and structured cloning appropriately.
Identify injection, prototype-pollution, retention, and performance risks.
Build and test a framework-free JavaScript application.

tasks.title: Build a Bounded Concurrent Retry Runner
tasks.description: Run async jobs with a concurrency limit, retries, and cancellation.
tasks.problemStatement: A batch runner must never exceed a configured number of active jobs and must preserve result order.
tasks.hint: Use a worker-pool pattern with a shared next index.
tasks.solutionCode: async function runBatch(jobs,{concurrency=2,retries=0,signal}={}){const results=new Array(jobs.length);let next=0;async function run(i){let attempt=0;while(true){if(signal?.aborted){results[i]={status:"cancelled"};return;}try{results[i]={status:"fulfilled",value:await jobs[i]()};return;}catch(error){if(attempt++>=retries){results[i]={status:"rejected",reason:error};return;}}}}async function worker(){while(true){const i=next++;if(i>=jobs.length)return;await run(i);}}await Promise.all(Array.from({length:Math.min(concurrency,jobs.length)},worker));return results;}
tasks.solutionExplanation: The pool limits active workers while per-job retry state remains local to each job.

async function openRepo(){const req=indexedDB.open("notes",1);req.onupgradeneeded=()=>req.result.createObjectStore("items",{keyPath:"id"});const db=await requestPromise(req);return{list:()=>requestPromise(db.transaction("items").objectStore("items").getAll()),put:item=>{const tx=db.transaction("items","readwrite");tx.objectStore("items").put(item);return new Promise((res,rej)=>{tx.oncomplete=res;tx.onerror=()=>rej(tx.error)})},close:()=>db.close()};}
tasks.solutionExplanation: The repository isolates IndexedDB’s event model and presents Promise-based methods.

lessons.title: Memory, Reachability, and Weak Collections
lessons.description: Reason about object lifetime despite automatic garbage collection.

notes.text: Garbage collection reclaims unreachable data, but application code can accidentally keep objects reachable through caches, closures, listeners, or global state. WeakMap/WeakSet can model associations that should not keep eligible object keys alive.

notes.text: eval parses and executes a string as JavaScript. Prototype pollution can arise from unsafe dynamic property paths or merges. Validate input and use structures that match the data semantics.

project.name: Offline Training Issue Tracker
project.description: A framework-free offline browser issue tracker using JavaScript modules, classes, IndexedDB, safe DOM rendering, async orchestration, and a worker analytics pipeline.
steps: Create the files represented in the code map.
Serve the project over HTTP and load app.js as a module.
Create and validate issues through the Issue class.
Persist snapshots through the IndexedDB repository.
Render issue text using DOM node APIs.
Use event delegation for progress/delete actions.
Run worker analytics from structured-cloned snapshots.
Run tests.js with Node.js and review the security/performance checklist.

code.index.html: Training Issue Tracker
code.js/render.js:
export function render(list,issues,action){list.replaceChildren();for(const issue of issues){const li=document.createElement("li"),title=document.createElement("h3"),p=document.createElement("p"),meta=document.createElement("p"),actions=document.createElement("div");li.dataset.id=issue.id;title.textContent=issue.title;p.textContent=issue.description;meta.textContent=`${issue.priority} · ${issue.status}`;for(const [kind,label] of [["progress","Progress"],["delete","Delete"]]){const b=document.createElement("button");b.type="button";b.dataset.action=kind;b.textContent=label;actions.append(b);}li.append(title,p,meta,actions);list.append(li);}list.onclick=e=>{const b=e.target.closest("button[data-action]"),li=b?.closest("li[data-id]");if(b&&li)action(b.dataset.action,li.dataset.id);}}
export const renderStats=(el,data)=>{el.textContent=JSON.stringify(data,null,2)};
code.tests.js:
import assert from "node:assert/strict";import {Issue,ValidationError} from "./js/domain.js";import {initial,add,update,remove,filter,visible,stats} from "./js/state.js";
const issue=new Issue({id:"1",title:"First",priority:"high"});assert.throws(()=>new Issue({title:""}),ValidationError);let s=add(initial(),issue);assert.equal(s.issues.length,1);s=update(s,"1",{status:"done"});assert.equal(s.issues[0].status,"done");s=filter(s,"first");assert.equal(visible(s).length,1);assert.deepEqual(stats(s.issues),{total:1,byStatus:{done:1},byPriority:{high:1}});s=remove(s,"1");assert.equal(s.issues.length,0);console.log("tests passed");

project.explanation: The architecture keeps deterministic state and domain logic separate from browser side effects. The repository isolates IndexedDB, rendering avoids HTML injection, and analytics run in a worker. This makes the project a practical assessment of the language rather than a framework tutorial.
